title: What If the World Never Switched to LED Bulbs?

scenes.text: What if we'd never switched to LED bulbs? Your power bill would be the smallest problem.
Lighting still uses about 8 percent of the world's electricity, roughly 2,200 terawatt hours a year. That's with LEDs.
A halogen bulb makes about 20 lumens per watt. A typical LED today makes close to 100. The best make 230.
Without that gain, homes would burn over 500 extra terawatt hours a year. That's about South Korea's entire electricity demand.
Shops and offices would need another 800 terawatt hours. That's more than all of Africa uses.
Indoor lighting would use roughly 70 percent more power. One humble bulb swap became a huge energy win.

description:
What if the world had never switched to LED bulbs?
Without LEDs, lighting inside buildings would use roughly 70 percent more electricity, according to the International Energy Agency.
